- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots downward; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast for 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.2) and price is trending down, model often underestimates further decline; increase forecast downward by 1–3% to align with mean reversion.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; for sentiment volatility >0.3, apply smoothing: average last 3 sentiment values before forecasting.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict early in the window; adjust by subtracting 1–2% from first 5 forecast points.
- When sentiment is high but price is falling, model often fails to recognize reversal; add a “sentiment decay” rule: if sentiment >0.7 and price drops >1%, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment drops below 0.5.
